title: Present Tense
description: Learn to talk about things that happen now or regularly.
competenceGoals: use simple verb forms in English

content.content:
## Present Tense - What Happens Now

The present tense tells us about things that happen now or things that happen regularly (every day, every week).

content.title: Present Tense
content.content:
**Present tense** tells us:
- What happens NOW: "I eat an apple."
- What happens REGULARLY: "I eat breakfast every morning."

**When to use:**
- "I play football every Saturday." (regular)
- "The sun shines." (right now)
- "Birds fly." (always true)

content.title: The S-Rule
content.content:
**Important rule:** When we use he, she, or it, we add **-s** to the verb!

**I, you, we, they** - no change:
- I play
- You play
- We play
- They play

**He, she, it** - add -s:
- He play**s**
- She play**s**
- It play**s**

content.title: Example: Using the S-Rule
content.problem:
Fill in the verb "like":
"I _____ ice cream. My sister _____ ice cream too."
content.solution:
"I **like** ice cream. My sister **likes** ice cream too."

**Why?**
- "I" - no change, so "like"
- "My sister" = "she" - add s, so "likes"

content.title: Watch Out!
content.content:
Some verbs change more when we add -s:

- go → go**es** (He goes to school)
- do → do**es** (She does homework)
- watch → watch**es** (He watches TV)
- have → **has** (She has a dog)

If the verb ends in -o, -s, -sh, -ch, or -x, add **-es**!

exercise.task: Write three sentences about what you do every day. Use present tense.
exercise.solution: Example: "I wake up at seven. I eat breakfast. I go to school."

content.content:
## Oppsummering

I dette kapittelet har du lært:

- **Present tense**: We use it for things that happen now or regularly.
- **The -s rule**: With he, she or it we add -s to the verb: he plays.
- **No change**: With I, you, we and they the verb does not change.

### Hugs!
- He, she, it - add an -s!
- I/you/we/they - no -s.

exercise.task: 'He ___ to school every day.' Which word fits?
When do we add -s to the verb?
Write the correct present tense of 'to read' for: I, she, they.
exercise.solution: I read, she reads, they read. Only 'she' (he/she/it) gets the -s.
hints: I and they do not change.
